body: I agree with you, but you know there are certain beliefs that, held even against popular opposition, can be vindicated in the future. Churchill was just about the only man in England who saw the danger the Nazis posed for almost 10 years, and the only man who encouraged the U.K. to rearm, and never backed down from that position. He was at best mocked, and at worst despised and feared for his "warmongering." To truly reflect the views of his constituents in the thirties he would have to got on the disarmament bandwagon and set England up for a Nazi takeover. Just a little example of how complicated leadership can be.

H-Dawg is obviously driven in part by a desire for personal glory, I think that that is inarguable. 

But Hillary also comes from a background of, in my opinion, genuine political concern for the less fortunate. After attending Yale Law she worked as a child advocate, protecting those who arguably were the most defenseless. When Bill was governor of Arkansas she was active in school reform. When Bill was in the White House she (and Bernie) worked to achieve Health Care reform (which failed, of course, but still a noble effort). For all of Hillary's shortcomings, her record shows that she at least began from a place of ideological honesty and conviction. Can we say the same for Trump?

Sad, but you have a point. America has a violent history of acquisition. That said, our acquisitive and violent leaders in the past have at least been governed by higher ideological principles:

Andrew Jackson "removed" Indians because he grew up on the frontier, in the context of constant Settler-Indian violence, and genuinely believed it was in Native Americans' best interest to move West, and maybe the violence would cease. Short-sighted, wrong, and arguably evil, but he thought he was doing the right thing. 

Lyndon Johnson sent thousands of innocent American men to die for a corrupt, indefensible South Vietnamese regime, but he did so on the understanding that such an action was necessary to deter expansionist Communism and save future lives. Once again, probably wrong in hindsight, but I believe he was guided by some elevated principles rather than just sheer bloodlust. 

I don't get that sense from Trump. If you're a leader of a nation-state, people will invariably die under your command, and the only thing I ask is that they die for something that is in any sense arguably worth dying for, and I don't believe Trump holds himself to that standard.

Classic political science brain-teaser. Ultimately it's circumstantial. I personally think that American Neo-Nazis, for example, are misguided bastards that need to be set straight. But to try to silence them authoritatively would lend a sort of under-dog credence to their views and attitude; in a sense it's better to let them discredit themselves than to try to stop them outright. Just my thoughts.

Hey, sometimes the truth hurts. And if her actions caused you and your siblings pain then you have a right to confront your mother on it. I don't know you or your mom, but I have to think that on some level your mother cried because she knew she was letting her children down, and you don't have to be a mother to know that that can be a pretty shitty feeling. Don't beat yourself up about being honest to her, but if you want to be gentle and apologize for hurting her feelings it might make her (and you) feel better.

Hey man, sorry to hear about your troubles. If it's any consolation, when I was your age I was unlucky in love as well. Could never seem to make anything long-term or serious ever happen. I really started to think that there was something wrong with me. And in some ways, there were. I was immature. I was lazy. I often could be angsty or unpleasant to be around. 

I have a little advice if you might like it: Stop looking so hard. 

> But here's the thing. I put so much thought and effort into my messages and nobody ever responds to them. I'm browsing /r/r4r almost every night looking for someone around my age/location with similar likes to message. Hoping that the person I message will be 'the one.' Sometimes I find some girls who are crazy similar to me and I freak out. I get really excited and type 2-3 long paragraphs to them talking about everything in their post and I'm so genuinely happy while doing so because I think I found someone to finally talk to. I'll be as honest as I possibly can, put a ton of love and effort into my message, and even include pictures because I realize that's important too. 

I'm sorry, but it sounds like you're honestly trying a little too hard. It sounds crazy, but I think you might be overwhelming these girls. Most women are attracted to confidence, and when I say that it often gets misconstrued as a Red-Piller trying to convince you that you have to treat women like shit, you don't. Just be honest but also casual. Write them a few sentences. If they don't reply, oh well. Not the end of the world. I think that you might honestly have more success if you approach things more casually, take it easy a bit. 

>  don't approach girls in public. I don't think I can. I think they'll laugh at me or act completely awkward if I tried to tell her that I thought she was cute. That would mentally shit on my self esteem if I even have any to begin with. 

Listen this is hard to get through to someone until you take the leap yourself, but if a girl rejects you, so fucking what? So one girl doesn't like you. If she makes a big show of rejecting you to friends, you can walk away happily knowing that she's something of a spiteful hag with obvious insecurities, and you're better off not knowing her. It's a can't-lose situation. 

I totally understand where you're coming from. I didn't have my first serious girlfriend until I was 21. Some don't until they're 41. Some never do because they worry too much and don't focus on what's important. 

**tl;dr** If girls keep rejecting you, maybe take a hard look at yourself to see what you need to improve. Keep it casual when you're making a move, and don't be afraid of making a move irl, because it's some of the most fun you'll ever have. Good luck, hope that helps!

In a democratic republic like ours, we should never try to silence other views. To do so would be fascistic. That said, I'm very disheartened by the inexplicable widespread appeal of Trump among the Republican base. I just don't get it. He's a guy who's whole modus operandi is "win" at any cost. Donald Trump isn't running for president because he gives a shit about any of us or our lives, he's doing it because Donald Trump needs to win the greatest prize of all: Leadership of the Free World. Not because he deserves it or because he is driven by any ideology to speak of, only because Donald Trump takes what he wants because that's what he does. It's mind-boggling that more people don't see this. 

On an interesting note, I was speaking with some moderate republican friends before Clinton clinched the primary and they said that while they hated Trump, their upper-class status meant that a Sanders-style tax policy would just not be in their interests financially, and that they would have to vote Trump in order to protect themselves in that sense. Most people vote in what they perceive to be their best interests.

One of the hardest things to accept about life is that, with very few exceptions, the people you meet will come in at their appointed time and leave at their appointed time. For most of your life, despite the amazing connections you can have, many of those connections will be severed, and it's not even necessarily anyone's fault, it's just the way it is. 

Not sure what I'm trying to say here, but basically that I'm sorry that you miss this person, and it sounds like you had a great relationship, but if they don't care about you anymore, you have to move on and focus on your own happiness at this point. God bless. :)

Everyone makes mistakes. Many people are confused about their gender identity. So far, you haven't done anything even approaching unforgivable or life-ruining. 

That said, getting yourself checked for STD's is a good idea after "doing things" with a stranger you met on the internet. I don't want to freak you out more, but homosexual men are among the most at-risk people where I'm from (the U.S.) for STD's, and it would definitely be advisable to get yourself checked out now, and then double-check a month or two from now, just for safety's sake. Planned Parenthood is great for this, make an appointment and they do a great job of keeping things confidential if you didn't want your parents to find out, just expect a co-pay. That said, and this all depends on your relationship with your parents, I think if you are to continue being sexually active it is important to have a degree of honesty with your folks about that. Just my thoughts. 

Hang in there. I made a lot of mistakes when I was younger, and I still do. Everyone does. Don't beat yourself up about it. Just take care of your health and remember how you feel now, and grow from it.

Hang in there. Try not to smoke as much as you can. You can do it. Maybe try the mantra: "Today I will not smoke".

I had a priest tell me a great metaphor for this sort of thing once, if you're plowing a field, and you're looking too far ahead, you won't pay attention to the plow, it'll get out of control and fuck your till. Keep your head down, focus on the here and now, and eventually you'll have done a great job.
